review_kind: Intensive second review of uncorroborated registry convictions
method: Static source and archive reconstruction; no sample code executed.

evidence: Inspected all 18 archive members. The nested source is a create-next-app landing page with local SVG assets, a font loader, stylesheet, and standard build configuration.
Outer main/start references index.js, which is absent. No outer install hooks, executable source, credential access, process execution, or exfiltration code is present.
The only lockfile install-script flag belongs to fsevents; all 375 resolved dependency URLs use registry.npmjs.org. Declared packages are not executed or vendored payloads in this artifact.
ICO has four valid declared image spans ending exactly at EOF; SVGs contain only vector paths.
Tea manifests and unrelated dependency fanout may indicate reward farming or low-quality publication, but do not establish trojanization or a recognized malware identity.
samples.limits: Declared dependency implementations and historical deployment are not supplied; this verdict is about the shipped artifact, not a guarantee about dependency versions.

evidence: Outer function defines an infinite Invoke-Bot loop. If activated and its guards permit operation, it downloads Twitter timeline XML, extracts status text, selects a pipe-delimited verb, and dispatches handlers.
!run takes received tweet text after the prefix, builds cmd.exe /C, and invokes it. !downexec downloads script text and passes it to a child PowerShell through Invoke-Expression.
!upload reads an operator-selected local file, Base64 encodes it, and posts it to pastebin.ca. !credential prompts for a password and records the plaintext username/password object.

!persist downloads script content to ProgramData/cache.db, constructs a hidden encoded PowerShell startup-link target, and saves a shortcut under a Startup folder. The decoded command is: $A = GC $env:ProgramData\cache.db; IEX $A. The other encoded constant is only the EICAR test string.

Implemented BindShell accepts TCP input and relays it to a cmd.exe process; GetSystem enables SeDebugPrivilege and duplicates the LSASS token onto a thread; KeyLog polls keyboard state, translates keys, attributes the foreground window, and appends records.

Public conference attribution, engagement IP guards, work hours, and a kill date support legitimate assessment use. Nevertheless the code implements a remotely directed trojan, local-file export, concealed persistence, and credential capture; without authorized deployment context an engineer should treat it as an offensive implant.
samples.limits: No top-level call invokes Invoke-TwitterBot. Its fixed 2013-02-16 kill date exits before networking if called today. KeyLog/GetSystem/BindShell implementations have mismatched switch handler names (KeylogCommand/GetSystemCommand/BindShellCommand); propagation has no implementation. Some URLs/APIs are obsolete, startup TargetPath includes arguments rather than separating them, and packet capture/job scope has defects. These are static capabilities, not claims of successful execution on a victim.

evidence: UTF-8 decodes FromBase64String($payload), constructs ScriptBlock.Create($decoded), then invokes that same ScriptBlock through & $sb.
$payload is never supplied, initialized, fetched, or embedded. There are no URLs, network calls, persistence, credential access, native memory operations, or attack-specific concealment.
The variable input could carry arbitrary code, but Base64 transport and dynamic script evaluation alone do not establish a hostile payload. Standalone execution has no payload to run.
samples.limits: The caller and value of $payload are unknown; a malicious supplied value would change the assessment.

changes: Retired three hostile Tea packaging/campaign rules; retained the archive layout as notable metadata without an attack or family claim.

Moved Base64/ScriptBlock co-occurrence into notable metaprogramming, preserving its scope, proximity, and exclusions. Split invocation into a constructed-evaluation observation that binds the immediately assigned and called variable.
Retired the independent Base64/WebClient hostile cradle composite; the encoded command reads a local file while other handlers download scripts, so the claimed Base64-wrapped download is false.
Disabled the misleading third-party Webdownload rule (its any-of branch matches ordinary Base64 text decoding); native decoding and HTTP traits retain those capabilities.

Added Twitter XML shell-task dispatch coverage gated on parsed shell/download/upload switch clauses, endpoint, XML fetch, message split, and evaluation; ordinary Twitter clients and local-only tables are controls.

Consolidated the inactive PowerShell kind:call constructor matcher into the existing canonical constructor-text trait and updated its consumers. The old abstract call node names do not include the grammar spelling invokation_expression. Removed the resulting redundant constructor OR alias; inert/quoted controls verify no unsupported convictions.
No severity changes to the accurately matched bind-shell, keystroke recording, or LSASS-token impersonation behaviors.
